protocols.title: Sleep schedule
protocols.purpose: Give sleep and wake time a steady anchor.
protocols.instructions: Choose a realistic wake time and keep it broadly consistent. Let bedtime move earlier or later with actual sleepiness rather than forcing time awake in bed.
protocols.minimum_version: Keep tomorrow's wake time within one hour of today's.
protocols.standard_version: Keep wake time within about 30 minutes on most days and protect enough time for sleep.
protocols.safety_notes: Persistent insomnia, breathing pauses, severe daytime sleepiness, or unusual sleep changes deserve clinical evaluation.

sources.title: Recommended amount of sleep for a healthy adult

protocols.title: Morning light
protocols.purpose: Give the body clock a consistent daytime signal.
protocols.instructions: Spend time outdoors soon after waking. Use ordinary daylight and keep looking naturally around the environment; do not stare at the sun.
protocols.standard_version: Spend 10–20 minutes outdoors within about an hour of waking, adjusting for weather and season.
protocols.safety_notes: Never look directly at the sun. Follow local advice for extreme heat, glare, or poor air quality.

sources.title: Light, sleep, and circadian rhythms
sources.publisher: National Institute of General Medical Sciences

protocols.title: Caffeine timing
protocols.purpose: Keep useful alertness while protecting sleep opportunity.
protocols.instructions: Notice your usual bedtime and set a personal caffeine cutoff early enough that it does not disturb sleep. Count coffee, tea, energy drinks, and pre-workout.
protocols.minimum_version: Move the last caffeinated drink one hour earlier today.
protocols.standard_version: Avoid caffeine for roughly 8 hours before planned sleep, adjusting for sensitivity.
protocols.safety_notes: Caffeine affects people differently. Consider pregnancy, anxiety, heart rhythm problems, medication interactions, and total dose with a clinician.

sources.title: Caffeine effects on sleep when consumed before bedtime

protocols.title: Zone 2 aerobic work
protocols.purpose: Build repeatable aerobic capacity with manageable fatigue.
protocols.instructions: Choose a low-impact activity and keep the effort conversational but purposeful. Use the talk test rather than chasing a perfect heart-rate number.
protocols.minimum_version: Walk or cycle easily for 10 minutes.
protocols.standard_version: Accumulate 30–45 minutes at a conversational effort two to four times per week.
protocols.safety_notes: Stop for chest pain, faintness, unusual breathlessness, or acute pain. Build gradually if currently inactive.

protocols.title: Strength practice
protocols.purpose: Maintain or build strength through repeatable resistance training.
protocols.instructions: Use controlled exercises, leave a little effort in reserve, and record sets, reps, load, and pain. Add work only when recovery and technique support it.
protocols.minimum_version: Complete one controlled working set of a safe movement.
protocols.standard_version: Train the major movement patterns two or three times weekly with a plan that can be repeated.
protocols.best_time: When alert and able to recover
protocols.safety_notes: Use appropriate technique and equipment. Pain, injury, or a medical condition may require professional guidance.

protocols.title: Walking
protocols.purpose: Add low-friction movement that supports health and mood.
protocols.instructions: Take a comfortable walk outside or indoors. Use short walks after meals or between work blocks when that makes consistency easier.
protocols.standard_version: Accumulate 20–30 minutes on most days, in one walk or several small walks.
protocols.best_time: After a meal or during a work break
protocols.safety_notes: Choose a safe route and pace. Stop for new severe pain, dizziness, or concerning symptoms.

protocols.title: Slow breathing
protocols.purpose: Create a short, practical downshift during stress.
protocols.instructions: Breathe comfortably and make the exhale slightly longer than the inhale for a few minutes. Stop if you feel light-headed.
protocols.standard_version: Practice 5 minutes at a relaxed pace once or twice daily.
protocols.best_time: Before a stressful task or at a transition
protocols.safety_notes: Do not force breath holds or deep breathing. Return to normal breathing if uncomfortable.

sources.title: Brief structured respiration practices enhance mood and reduce physiological arousal

protocols.title: Simple meditation
protocols.purpose: Practice returning attention without needing a perfect mind.
protocols.instructions: Sit comfortably, choose a neutral anchor such as breath or sound, and gently return attention whenever you notice it wandered.
protocols.minimum_version: Sit for two minutes and notice three breaths.
protocols.standard_version: Practice 10 minutes, five days per week.
protocols.safety_notes: Meditation is not a substitute for mental-health care. Stop and seek support if practice consistently worsens distress.

protocols.title: Sauna session
protocols.purpose: Use heat as a controlled relaxation and recovery practice.
protocols.instructions: Use a familiar sauna for a short comfortable round, hydrate, and leave before feeling unwell. Recovery matters more than a target temperature.
protocols.standard_version: Use 10–20 minute rounds one to three times per week if tolerated.
protocols.best_time: A time with hydration and recovery afterward
protocols.safety_notes: Avoid alcohol and dehydration. Extra caution is needed with pregnancy, low blood pressure, heart conditions, or medications that affect heat tolerance; ask a clinician.

protocols.title: Gentle cold exposure
protocols.purpose: Experiment with a brief alerting stimulus without turning discomfort into a test of worth.
protocols.instructions: Finish a normal shower with a brief cool period and return to warmth. Keep breathing normally and use a controlled environment.
protocols.minimum_version: 10 seconds of cool water at the end of a shower.
protocols.standard_version: Build toward 30–60 seconds one to three times per week if comfortable.
protocols.best_time: A time when you can warm up safely afterward
protocols.safety_notes: Do not use open water alone. Avoid if cold exposure is medically unsafe; stop for chest pain, severe shivering, numbness, or breathing difficulty.

sources.title: Cold-water immersion: a review of health and performance evidence

protocols.title: Protein at meals
protocols.purpose: Make adequate protein easier through ordinary meals.
protocols.instructions: Include a clear protein source in one or more meals, using foods that fit your preferences, budget, culture, and dietary needs.
protocols.minimum_version: Add one protein-containing food to one meal.
protocols.standard_version: Include a protein source at two or three meals and review energy, digestion, and preference.
protocols.safety_notes: Individual needs vary. Kidney disease, allergies, pregnancy, or a medically prescribed diet warrant professional advice before changing intake substantially.

sources.title: International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: protein and exercise
sources.publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

protocols.title: Reading time
protocols.purpose: Create a calmer path to learning or winding down.
protocols.instructions: Keep one book visible and read without multitasking. Paper or e-ink can be useful near bedtime if it does not delay sleep.
protocols.standard_version: Read for 15–20 minutes on most days.
protocols.safety_notes: Choose content and lighting that do not increase distress or interfere with sleep.

sources.title: How are habits formed: modelling habit formation in the real world

protocols.title: Social connection
protocols.purpose: Protect regular contact with people who matter.
protocols.instructions: Send a thoughtful message, make a call, share a meal, or spend unhurried time with someone. Depth matters more than a score.
protocols.standard_version: Make two or three meaningful contacts each week.
protocols.safety_notes: Respect boundaries and personal safety. Connection should not require staying in harmful relationships.

sources.title: Our epidemic of loneliness and isolation

protocols.title: Single-task focus block
protocols.purpose: Make one meaningful task easier to start and finish.
protocols.instructions: Choose one visible outcome, remove the phone from reach, set a modest timer, and stop or take a real break when it ends.
protocols.minimum_version: Work on one task for 10 minutes.
protocols.standard_version: Complete one 25–50 minute single-task block on workdays.
protocols.safety_notes: Take breaks for eyes, posture, hydration, and movement. Do not use focus blocks to ignore urgent health or safety needs.

protocols.title: Mobility break
protocols.purpose: Interrupt long sitting and practice comfortable range of motion.
protocols.instructions: Move slowly through comfortable hip, ankle, shoulder, or upper-back positions. Use breathing and control rather than forcing range.
protocols.standard_version: Practice 10 minutes five days per week or use short movement breaks throughout the day.
protocols.best_time: Between long sitting periods or before training
protocols.safety_notes: Stay within a comfortable range and stop for sharp, radiating, or worsening pain.

sources.title: Physical activity and sedentary behaviour guidelines
